name: Ahihud
overview: Ahihud was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Gera. His mention is concise and primarily genealogical, situating him within the Benjaminite lineage. There are no additional notes or extended narratives about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahihud means '[my] brother has majesty,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name with a meaningful designation. This name is not indicated as given directly by God, but it carries a sense of honor or dignity within the family context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Ahihud as the son of Gera, anchoring him firmly within the Benjaminite family line. No other family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Ahihud's significance lies in his role within the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin, contributing to the biblical account of Israel's tribal families. His identification as Gera's son helps preserve the heritage and continuity of the Benjaminite lineage, which is important for understanding the tribal divisions and ancestral lines in Israel. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of Scripture in recording the descendants of Israel.
